input.description: Northside Electric Co-op (sample). Monthly bill for residential electric service at her apartment.

reviews.quote: Shelter includes room, rent, mortgage payments, real property taxes, heating fuel, gas, electricity, water, sewerage, and garbage collection services.

reason.plain: Yes, this is a shelter cost. Electricity is on the regulation's list of shelter items, so someone else paying it counts as in-kind support.
reason.technical: 20 CFR 416.1130(b)(1) lists "electricity" among the items included in shelter. It also says ISM considers shelter "that you receive because someone else pays for it." A third party paying the electric co-op directly is therefore in-kind shelter. Under 416.1103(g), the payment itself is not income, but what the recipient receives because of it is. The FR 2024-06464 rule confirms that shelter expenses, including electricity, remain in ISM after September 30, 2024.

reviews.quote: In household LA's, shelter costs (also known as “items of shelter” ) are mortgage payments, property insurance (if required by a mortgageholder), rent, gas, electricity, heating fuel, water, sewer, garbage collection service, and real property taxes.

reason.plain: Yes, this is a shelter cost. Electricity for her home is on the manual's list of shelter costs, so someone else paying it counts as in-kind support.
reason.technical: SI 00835.020B.36 lists "electricity" among the shelter costs. SI 00835.465D.1 and SI 00815.400A confirm the rule: a third-party payment to the vendor is not itself income, but the shelter received as a result is ISM.

referee.summary: Both reviewers found it in their own rulebook: this bill is a housing cost.
